Your team projects 69.0 with Haaland captained and Bench Boost played this week. That chip is 3.6 points better deployed now than later.

Salah carries a knock with a 75% chance of playing. He is your second-most valuable asset and only 0.3 points behind the armband, so losing him would sting. Haaland remains the captain—he has clearer fitness and the gap is small enough that the armband should stay where it is. If Salah fails to play, you have no meaningful cover on the bench; Anderson and Muniz project 2.9 and 2.4 respectively.

The model recommends Wood out for Watkins, netting 5.1 points after a 4-point hit. You have no free transfer, so the cost is real. Watkins projects 9.1 ahead of Wood over the horizon, which is substantial, but you are taking those 4 points of damage today to get there.

Your three Arsenal players and pairing of Liverpool and Manchester City assets create some concentration, but Bench Boost dilutes the downside of any single underperformance. Mykolenko on the bench is flagged doubtful; if Salah is out and Mykolenko does not play, you would be forced to field a fourth midfielder or accept a blank, so monitor both through the week.

Your team projects 60.8 points this week, rising to 69.0 with the captain on Haaland. The main concern is Salah's knock: he has a 75% chance of playing, but if he doesn't, you have no cover on the bench—Mykolenko is flagged doubtful himself, and Anderson and Muniz project below 3 points. Holding Salah as captain has merit given his projection and his likelihood of involvement, though Haaland is only 0.3 clear and offers more certainty.

The model recommends replacing Wood with Watkins for a net gain of 5.1 points after the 4-point hit. Watkins projects 0.9 higher than Wood over the horizon, which is modest, but the move improves your forward line and spreads risk given Arsenal's three-player concentration. You have no free transfers, so this uses a hit.

The Bench Boost is worth 14.2 points this week—3.6 ahead of any other week available. Your bench is weak (10.7 projected), but Mykolenko's doubtful flag makes timing uncertain anyway. If you're confident in playing it now, the edge is clear; if you wait and Mykolenko clears, you might do better next week.

The model's record is currently -13 net points, suggesting caution, though that reflects past decisions rather than this week's advice. Your main risk is Salah's fitness.

Your eleven projects 60.8 this week, or 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. He is 0.3 clear of Salah, though Salah carries a knock with a 75% chance of playing—if he doesn't, the captain choice matters less. Mykolenko on the bench is flagged doubtful at 25% likely to play, but with Semenyo, Anderson and Muniz as backups, you have cover.

The model recommends Wood to Watkins, a move that costs a 4-point hit but nets 5.1 over the horizon. Watkins projects 9.1 more than Wood across the fixture run. The trade-off is fine if you trust the longer view, though you have no free transfers to play with and only £0.5m in the bank.

Bench Boost is worth 14.2 this week—3.6 better than waiting. Your bench is thin (10.7 projected), but that gain is large enough to justify playing it now rather than chasing a better week.

Three Arsenal players and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City gives you heavy exposure to those clubs. The model's track record is -13 net points across 11 decisions, so trust it cautiously, but this week's setup—a strong captain choice, a transfer that pays off, and a timely chip—looks solid on paper.
